Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` fails because the method `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` returns true for entries that have Unix permissions with multiple flags set. The method `isUnixSymlink()` checks whether the Unix mode bits include exactly the symbolic link flag by the expression `(getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`. 

`getUnixMode()` returns the mode bits extracted from the external attributes if the platform is Unix (`(int) ((getExternalAttributes() >> SHORT_SHIFT) & SHORT_MASK)`). The symbolic link flag is defined as `0120000` (octal). The test checks an entry that in reality is not a symlink but likely has multiple flags set represented by a mode like `177777` (octal), which includes the `LINK_FLAG` bits but also additional bits. Because of the current bitwise test, the method returns true as long as the `LINK_FLAG` bits are set, regardless of other bits.

Thus, the core issue is that `isUnixSymlink()` uses a bitwise AND to test for presence of the symlink bit without verifying if only the symlink bit is set and no others. This results in false positives for entries with more than one flag set in their Unix mode bits. This matches the problem described in the bug report, which states that entries with permission bits like `177777` return true for isUnixSymlink incorrectly.

Recent bug reports do not contain useful related information for this issue.

The root cause is that `isUnixSymlink()` logic is overly permissive by checking `(mode & LINK_FLAG) == LINK_FLAG` instead of stricter mode matching or masking out irrelevant bits before comparison. It should instead check if the mode indicates a symlink file type exactly, not just the presence of the symlink flag bits amidst others.

Best fix location will be inside `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` method.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
